repoMap: Sasha's Meal Companion is a phone-first Next.js/TypeScript PWA for one user (Sasha, ulcerative colitis: no gluten/dairy/apple) built on Supabase (auth + Postgres + storage), currently mid-way through an 8-phase build (phases 0-7 landed, phase 8 not started). The App Router (app/) holds pages (foods, recipes, scan, settings, week, sign-in) and API routes under app/api/ for sync (ops/changes), foods/barcode/search, health (daily/ingest/oura/tokens), coach (AI chat threads), log (commit/propose), media, export, proposals, targets, and background jobs (backup, estimate, media-sweep, oura-pull, weekly-proposal, weekly-review) plus an MCP server route. lib/ is the domain core: the hand-curated diet-safety rule set (foods.ts, meals.ts, scaling.ts, plan.ts, targets.ts, rotation.ts) that tests guard directly; a USDA/OFF food catalog and search-ranking stack (catalog/, food-db.ts, search/); barcode scanning with OCR/decoder quorum voting (barcode/); an AI capture/coach layer that turns photos or chat into logged meals (ai/, capture/, coach/); a client-authoritative op-log sync engine with outbox/merge/fingerprint (sync/) sitting alongside a legacy Supabase sync path being retired; server-only boundary code for auth, rate limiting, privileged/service-role access, and encrypted health-token handling (server/); a health-data and Oura-OAuth ingest pipeline (health/, oura/) feeding a TDEE/expenditure estimator and weekly proposal engine (expenditure.ts, tdee.ts, proposal.ts); and export/backup/migration utilities. components/ holds the NeuForm-design-system UI (meal cards, macro gauges, capture sheets, recipe/favorites builders, health dashboard, coach chat). supabase/migrations/ has ~29 sequential SQL files spanning catalog, sync, RLS, RPC, health, Oura OAuth, coach, expenditure, and body-profile schema. Tests are vitest, colocated as *.test.ts/*.test.tsx next to source, and CI/PR policy (per AGENTS.md) is run-once, targeted-rerun-on-failure — no full suite reruns.

confirmed.title: bannedReason misses buttermilk and malt (dairy/gluten false negatives)
confirmed.evidence: The gluten check `/wheat|\bbread\b|pasta|barley|\brye\b|couscous|seitan|flour tortilla/` (line 146-147) has no 'malt' term, and the dairy check `/\bmilk\b|cheese|yogurt|yoghurt|\bbutter\b|\bghee\b|whey|casein|cream\b|ice cream/` (line 148-149) uses `\bmilk\b`/`\bbutter\b` word-boundary patterns that do not match inside a compound word with no internal boundary. Verified directly: `bannedReason("Buttermilk")` -> null, `bannedReason("Buttermilk pancakes")` -> null, `bannedReason("Malt vinegar")` -> null, `bannedReason("Malt extract")` -> null. This same function is the sole gate for two live write paths: components/AddFoodSheet.tsx:123 (`canSave = ... && !banned`, a hard block only when bannedReason is non-null) and app/api/mcp/route.ts:92-93 (the AI coach's add-food tool: `const reason = bannedReason(name); if (reason) return text('Refused: ...')`).
confirmed.scenario: Sasha (or the AI coach, on her behalf) types 'Buttermilk pancakes' or 'Malt extract' into 'Something else' (AddFoodSheet) or has the coach add it via the MCP tool. bannedReason returns null, the Add button is enabled, and the food is saved with status 'eats' — it is then eligible for eatsByRole/rotationPool (lib/foods.ts:193-202, 321-347) and can be served to her in a real meal.
confirmed.impact: This is the one custom-entry safety gate for her colitis constraints (no gluten, no dairy). A false negative here is a direct path for a dairy or gluten item to enter her Eats list and then appear in her daily plan — the exact failure the four core-rule tests exist to prevent, but on a path (custom entry) none of those tests exercise.
confirmed.fix: Add 'malt' to the gluten pattern; change the dairy 'milk'/'butter' checks to match as a substring (or explicitly enumerate common compounds like buttermilk) rather than requiring a word boundary that a compound word defeats.
confirmed.testGap: lib/foods.test.ts:43-51 only exercises 'Whey isolate', 'Butter', 'Greek yogurt', 'Sourdough bread' — no compound-word case (buttermilk) and no malt case at all.

confirmed.title: Legacy days/foods sync is whole-record last-write-wins, not field-merged
confirmed.evidence: lib/server/db.ts:86-99 pushRecords' `days` branch: `const rows = body.days.filter((d) => !current.has(d.date) || newer(d.updatedAt, current.get(d.date)?.updatedAt)).map(...); await db().from("days").upsert(rows);` — the entire StoredDay row (extras, eaten, notes, swaps, gut, floorDay, waterMl) is replaced wholesale whenever the incoming updatedAt is later than the server's; there is no per-field merge and no optimistic-concurrency check (contrast with the new engine's apply_sync_op, which uses pg_advisory_xact_lock + base_rev compare-and-swap in supabase/migrations/20260919090300_phase3_sync_entities.sql:399-486). The identical pattern exists for `foods` at lib/server/db.ts:71-84 and `settings` at lib/server/db.ts:101-112.
confirmed.scenario: The live, documented MCP integration (docs/codex-setup.md, 'Log my gut as iffy today') calls the `log_gut` tool (app/api/mcp/route.ts:170-186) or `log_food` tool (app/api/mcp/route.ts:207-244), each of which does `const { days } = await pullAll(); const day = { ...(days[d] ?? {date:d}), gut: value (or extras: [...]), updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() }; await pushRecords({ days: [day] });`. Meanwhile Sasha's phone runs the legacy engine on every save (components/SyncBootstrap.tsx:22-24 still calls `syncNow()` from lib/sync.ts alongside the new `syncOnce()`, per the comment 'Legacy engine stays wired until integration Task I-3 deletes lib/sync.ts'). Any local interaction with the SAME calendar day — ticking a meal eaten, adding a food, setting a note, toggling floor day — goes through lib/store.ts:184-189 `updateDay`, which unconditionally rebuilds the WHOLE StoredDay from the phone's own (possibly stale) cached copy and stamps `updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()` on it, synchronously, before any network round trip. The 1.5s-debounced sync (lib/sync.ts:130-171 `syncNow`) then pushes `Object.values(local.days)` (every day, not just the touched one) to /api/sync. Because the local day's updatedAt is stamped at the moment of the tap (essentially always later than the coach's server-side write, which typically happened seconds to minutes earlier), lib/sync.ts:84-97 `mergeSnapshot`'s own pull-then-merge step also rejects the server's (coach's) version as 'not newer', so even the pull-before-push ordering inside one syncNow() cycle does not protect against it. The subsequent push therefore overwrites the server row with the phone's day object, which never contained the coach's addition — the gut check-in or logged meal the coach just wrote is silently and permanently gone, with no conflict, no error, and no trace anywhere in the app.
confirmed.impact: Silent, unrecoverable loss of health-tracking data (gut symptom logs, tied directly to her ulcerative colitis monitoring) or logged meals, any time the documented Codex/MCP coach integration and an ordinary phone interaction touch the same day within one sync window. This is exactly the 'lost writes' and 'wipe Sasha's logged days' failure mode this audit round was asked to hunt for, and it sits on the officially sanctioned, currently-live integration path (docs/codex-setup.md), not a hypothetical multi-device scenario.
confirmed.fix: Either (a) give lib/server/db.ts pushRecords' `days`/`foods`/`settings` branches a field-level merge (union extras/notes/swaps by key, newer-wins per field, the same shape lib/sync/merge.ts already implements for the new schema) instead of a whole-row replace, or (b) migrate the MCP tools (log_gut, log_food, add_food, set_food_status) off lib/server/db.ts onto the new op-log schema's apply_sync_op RPC, which already has the advisory-lock compare-and-swap this legacy path lacks — this is what 'release B' (the retired PR #18) was presumably meant to do; until one of these lands, the legacy engine should not be run concurrently with routine phone use on the same day.
confirmed.testGap: none — AGENTS.md's guarded rules (lib/foods.test.ts, lib/meals.test.ts) cover diet-safety invariants, not sync merge correctness; there is no test anywhere exercising a concurrent legacy-server write racing a phone push for the same StoredDay/food row.

votes.reason: Verified end-to-end, not just at the cited lines. (1) lib/server/db.ts:86-99 (and 71-84, 101-112) is confirmed whole-row upsert: pushRecords compares only a single top-level `updatedAt` per record and, if newer, writes the entire incoming object as `data`, with no per-field merge and no compare-and-swap — contrast with the new engine's field-wise `mergeEntity` (lib/sync/merge.ts) and advisory-locked RPC, which exist precisely because this problem is understood. (2) The MCP route confirmed to hit this exact path: app/api/mcp/route.ts's `log_gut` (~line 170) and `log_food` (~line 207) both do `pullAll()` then `{...(days[d] ?? {date:d}), <field>, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()}` then `pushRecords({days:[day]})` — a whole-day rebuild from a snapshot that can already be stale. (3) I initially doubted whether the "legacy" phone engine is still the UI's real data path, since Phase 0 added a newer IndexedDB-based engine (lib/sync/*) — but docs/plans/2026-09-10-phase-0/lane-C-sync.md line 23-24 states plainly that engine is "additive" and "the store switch ... belongs to the integration branch" (not done). Direct proof: app/page.tsx imports `loadStore/getDay/updateDay` from `lib/store.ts` (the legacy localStorage store) and calls `resolveDay(loadStore(), viewedDate)` at line 223/230 — this is what Sasha's Today screen actually renders and writes. app/page.tsx:336 calls `updateDay(viewedDate, { gut: value })` — the exact same `days[date].gut` field, exact same whole-record rebuild-and-restamp pattern (lib/store.ts:184-189 `updateDay`), that the MCP `log_gut` tool also writes. So the race is not hypothetical or against dead code: Sasha's own gut-check UI and the coach's MCP `log_gut` tool converge on the identical legacy Supabase row through two independent whole-row-replace paths. (4) SyncBootstrap.tsx (mounted in app/layout.tsx OUTSIDE AuthGate, so it runs on every load regardless of sign-in state) unconditionally calls legacy `syncNow()` alongside the new `syncOnce()`, with an explicit comment that the legacy engine "stays wired until integration Task I-3 deletes lib/sync.ts." (5) The production readiness audit (docs/readiness/2026-09-12-production-readiness.md, "Area 5" and the 18:07 UTC addendum) independently confirms the legacy `foods/days/settings` tables are the ones actually populated in production and that `SASHA_SYNC_TOKEN`/`SASHA_MCP_TOKEN` are both live production env vars; AGENTS.md's own phase table confirms "release B" (the PR meant to retire the legacy path) was closed, not merged, as of 2026-09-12, one day before HEAD. The one unverifiable link in the chain — whether Sasha's actual phone still carries the legacy `meal-companion:sync-token` in localStorage — cannot be proven from the repo alone, but the code's own comments, the still-live token env vars, and the fact that without that token neither her own edits nor the coach's MCP writes would ever reach the other device at all (defeating the entire purpose of the documented MCP "coach" integration) make it very unlikely the token is absent. The mechanics of the described loss (local tap after the coach's write, before the next pull absorbs it, so `updateDay`'s spread-from-stale-`existing` drops the just-added field, then a later-timestamped push overwrites the server) trace exactly through the cited functions with no gap or guard I could find.

confirmed.title: localStorage write failures silently revert every local write
confirmed.evidence: saveStore() (lines 158-173): `cached = next;` updates the in-memory store unconditionally, then `try { window.localStorage.setItem(...) } catch { /* silently no-op */ }`. loadStore() (lines 127-144) ignores `cached` and unconditionally re-reads from `window.localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)` on every call. app/page.tsx's Today() calls `const store = loadStore();` directly in its render body (line 223) on every render.
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced standalone (scratchpad/store-repro.mjs mirroring the exact save/load logic): once localStorage.setItem starts throwing (iOS Safari quota, private browsing, storage disabled), toggleEaten()/addExtra()/updateDay() all still call refresh() and the UI shows the tick/log as applied. But the very next render's `loadStore()` call re-reads the untouched (pre-write) localStorage blob and overwrites `cached`, silently reverting the change with no error, no retry and no diagnostic — confirmed: tick survived? false.
confirmed.impact: Once local storage starts failing — plausible on an iOS PWA that has accumulated captured-photo drafts, catalog cache, and months of daily logs — every subsequent write (ticking a meal, logging food, floor day, gut/weight check-ins, notes) appears to succeed for an instant and then silently disappears on the next render or app relaunch, with zero signal that anything went wrong. For a one-person health-tracking app this is exactly the kind of failure that quietly erodes trust in the data and can lose a day's gut/symptom log with no way to know it happened.
confirmed.fix: Have saveStore() return a success/failure result (or track a `persistFailed` flag) instead of unconditionally updating `cached`; surface a banner/toast on write failure the way DayTypeToggle.tsx already does for its own save path. Add a store.test.ts case that makes localStorage.setItem throw and asserts the next loadStore() does NOT silently discard the pending change.

confirmed.title: Rejected/blocked log commits leave a phantom entry in her visible log with no warning
confirmed.evidence: `confirmCatalogPortion` (components/LogFoodSheet.tsx:315-352) calls `onAdd(entry)` at line 327 — adding the item to her visible Today list — BEFORE awaiting `commitLogEntry`. When the server rejects the commit (e.g. `policyIssues` in lib/server/log.ts:378-394 returns `{status:"invalid", issues:[...]}` because `evaluatePolicy` found a blocked allergen/category), the only handling is `if (result.status !== "ok" && result.status !== "queued") { console.warn("[log] commit rejected", result.status, entryId); }` (lines 349-351) — no toast, no removal of the already-added local entry, no re-open of the sheet. The comment at lines 347-348 says "a rejected commit keeps the entry and says so in the console. Phase 3 turns this into a toast" — but AGENTS.md's phase table records Phase 3 as already landed (PR #41), so this stopgap shipped as final behavior.
confirmed.scenario: Continuing the previous scenario (or any catalog food that resolves to a `blocked` policy verdict, e.g. one of her own `avoid_food_ref_ids`): she logs it, the row appears immediately in "Also today" with full macros counted into her kcal/macro rings, but the server never persisted it (commit came back `invalid`). Nothing in the UI tells her this happened — only a `console.warn` she will never see on a phone.
confirmed.impact: Her locally-displayed daily totals and "logged" state permanently diverge from what the server actually stored, with zero indication anything went wrong — a phantom entry for a food that was supposed to be blocked specifically to protect her colitis. On any later sync/pull that reconciles from server truth, the entry (and its macros) can silently vanish from a day she already reviewed, or persist indefinitely in the local store since the outbox logic never retries an `invalid` result but also never undoes the optimistic `onAdd`.
confirmed.fix: On a non-ok, non-queued `commitLogEntry` result, remove or mark the optimistically-added entry and surface a blocking message to her (the promised Phase 3 toast), especially distinguishing `status: "invalid"` (policy-blocked, must not silently stay logged) from a transient failure.

confirmed.evidence: The route inserts a `job_runs` row with `status: "running"` (lines 44-52) and then calls `writeWeeklyReview` (line 54) with no enclosing try/catch around it; the only catch is the outer `catch (e) { return jsonError(e); }` (lines 59-61), which never updates `job_runs`. confirmed.scenario: writeWeeklyReview() calls runWeeklyReview() -> generateStructured(), which throws when the paid Gemini runtime is unavailable — documented as having actually happened in production the same day this code was committed (docs/ai-data-handling.md: "gemini-3.8-flash... exhausted all three application retries with 503 high demand"). When that happens on a Sunday weekly-review cron run, the `job_runs` row for `("weekly-review", userId, weekStart)` is left at `status: "running"` forever (no `finished_at`). confirmed.title: SW cache silently masks true offline state on Body dashboard
confirmed.evidence: public/sw.js:59-69 `networkFirst()` does `fetch(request).then(putInCache).catch(() => caches.match(request)...)` and line 97 routes every other same-origin GET (no `/api/` exclusion) through it, even though the file's own header comment (lines 4-6) says 'only network responses (HTML, JS/CSS chunks, icons, manifest) are cached here.' Meanwhile lib/health-client.ts:49-63 `fetchDaily()` calls `fetch('/api/health/daily?from=...&to=...', {cache:'no-store'})` and relies on the promise REJECTING to know she's offline (sets `offline:true`, skips `writeCachedDaily`). components/BodyDashboard.tsx:166-167 only renders 'Offline — last synced {lastSeen(fetchedAt)}.' when `offline` is true.
confirmed.scenario: Sasha opens /body once while online (SW caches the 200 response for that day's `from`/`to` query, which stays the same all day). Later that day her phone loses signal and she reopens /body. The SW's `fetch()` inside the worker fails, so `networkFirst` falls back to `caches.match(request)` and resolves with the STALE cached 200 response — the page's own `fetch()` never rejects, so `fetchDaily()`'s `catch` block never runs. The code takes the success path: it treats the stale JSON as fresh, calls `writeCachedDaily(response)` which overwrites `fetchedAt` with `now`, and returns `offline:false`.
confirmed.impact: Sasha sees old weight/sleep/expenditure numbers stamped with a fresh-looking timestamp and no 'Offline — last synced' banner, even though `lib/health-client.ts` was specifically built to show that banner. She has no way to tell the numbers are stale, which matters for a health dashboard she uses to judge her ramp/TDEE state.
confirmed.fix: Exclude `/api/` (or same-origin fetch requests with an `Accept: application/json` header) from the SW's cache-and-serve fallback — let those requests reject/504 on network failure like the `cacheFirst`/`navigate` paths already special-case, so the app-layer offline detection in health-client.ts (and any other JSON fetcher) keeps working as designed.

confirmed.evidence: The only test step in CI is `pnpm test` (== `vitest run`, package.json:11), run with no SUPABASE_TEST_URL / SUPABASE_TEST_ANON_KEY / SUPABASE_TEST_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY / SUPABASE_TEST_DB_URL set anywhere in the workflow. tests/helpers/supabase.ts:15-20 computes `HAS_BRANCH = URL.length>0 && ANON.length>0 && SECRET.length>0` from those exact env vars and its own doc comment says: 'Every suite in tests/ skips itself when SUPABASE_TEST_URL is unset, so CI stays green without a branch.' 41 of the 183 test files under tests/ gate themselves with `describe.skipIf(!HAS_BRANCH)` or the equivalent `const run = HAS_BRANCH ? describe : describe.skip`, including tests/rls/cross-user.test.ts:18 ('cross-user denial' across 29 user-owned tables), tests/rls/apply-sync-op.test.ts, tests/rls/security-invoker.test.ts, tests/sync/phase3-cross-user.test.ts:8, tests/sync/cross-user-http.test.ts, tests/log/cross-user.test.ts, tests/export/cross-user.test.ts, tests/mcp/token.test.ts, tests/search/cross-user.test.ts, and tests/search/rpc-security.test.ts. package.json:16 defines `test:integration` (`vitest run tests/ --no-file-parallelism`) specifically to run this suite, but no CI job (there is only ci.yml, with a `quality` and a `build` job) ever invokes it or sets the required env vars.
confirmed.scenario: A future migration or RLS policy change accidentally widens a policy (e.g. a `USING (true)` slip, or a service-role client leaking into a user-scoped query) on any of the 29 tables covered by tests/rls/cross-user.test.ts — including health_samples, coach_threads, api_tokens, weigh_ins. Every push and PR to main runs CI green, because the only test that would catch it is silently skipped (HAS_BRANCH is always false in CI). The regression reaches production and a second Supabase Auth user (once one exists) could read or write Sasha's rows.
confirmed.impact: For a single-user phone-first PWA carrying health data (ulcerative colitis history, weigh-ins, Oura tokens, coach threads), this is exactly the auth/RLS-bypass class of bug CI exists to prevent, and it is the one class of bug this CI configuration is structurally unable to catch on any commit. docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:36-37 confirms this is deliberate ('Database integration tests use an isolated Supabase preview branch. Reset it... before a release check') but that makes the safety net a manual, easy-to-forget step rather than an automatic gate.
confirmed.fix: Add a scheduled or PR-triggered CI job that provisions (or reuses) a Supabase test branch, exports SUPABASE_TEST_URL/ANON_KEY/SERVICE_ROLE_KEY/DB_URL, and runs `pnpm test:integration`. confirmed.title: Dedupe key omits device_label; same-hour multi-device HAE samples silently drop one device forever
confirmed.evidence: dedupe_key text generated always as (coalesce(vendor_sample_id, type || '|' || (extract(epoch from (start_time - timestamptz 'epoch')))::bigint::text || '|' || (extract(epoch from (end_time - timestamptz 'epoch')))::bigint::text)) stored); ... create unique index health_samples_dedupe on health_samples (user_id, source_id, dedupe_key); -- (line 29). lib/health/dedupe.ts:12-18 mirrors the same formula, also without device_label. lib/health/normalize.ts:82-84 (`const end = type === "body_mass" ? at : hourAfter(at); samples.push({ type, ...toCanonical(type, qty, unit), start_time: at, end_time: end, device_label: device, tz });`) always synthesizes a 1-hour window purely from the raw timestamp, independent of which device produced it. supabase/migrations/20260925000000_phase5_health_ingest.sql:92-116 shows the apply RPC: the `incoming` CTE does `distinct on (dedupe_key) order by dedupe_key, vendor_updated_at desc nulls last` (no further tiebreak), and the `on conflict (user_id, source_id, dedupe_key) do update ... where excluded.vendor_updated_at is not null and (...)` — HAE never sets vendor_updated_at, so once one device's row is written, every later row (or the other device's row in the same payload) with the same type+start+end permanently no-ops as `skipped`.
confirmed.scenario: Sasha's Health Auto Export (a single health_sources row, kind=health_auto_export) exports hourly-bucketed step_count/active_energy readings from both her Apple Watch and her iPhone (both present, both logging that hour — the common case, not an edge case). tests/health/normalize.test.ts's own HAE fixture (lines 7-9) has "Apple Watch" and "Sasha's iPhone" both reporting step_count for the same metric, just at different hours in the fixture — nothing in normalize.ts or the schema prevents them from sharing the same hour, which is the realistic case. When they do share an hour, both rows normalize to identical start_time/end_time (via hourAfter) and therefore identical dedupe_key (device_label is not part of the key), so only one device's reading is ever written; the other is silently and permanently skipped.
confirmed.impact: One device's step or active-energy reading for that hour is lost with no error surfaced anywhere Sasha would see (only an internal `skipped` count in the ingest response that no UI displays). This directly understates or overstates the numbers unionAttribution (lib/health/daily.ts) rolls up into `steps`/`active_kcal`, which feed Today's Body card and the TDEE/expenditure estimator — the exact scenario the intervals.ts Watch-preference union logic exists to handle correctly, defeated before it ever runs.
confirmed.fix: Fold device_label (or a normalized device/source identity) into the dedupe_key formula in both the SQL generated column and lib/health/dedupe.ts, and add a deterministic tiebreaker (e.g. device_label) to the `incoming` CTE's `distinct on` ordering so same-key rows within one payload resolve predictably instead of arbitrarily.
confirmed.testGap: tests/health/dedupe.test.ts and tests/health/migration-ingest.test.ts/integration.test.ts never test two different device_label samples sharing identical type+start_time+end_time within one source; tests/health/daily.test.ts only exercises the union/overlap-preference logic with staggered (non-colliding) start/end windows, never the exact-match collision the DB actually produces for hourly HAE data.

I then read the actual installed `@supabase/postgrest-js@2.116.0` source and confirmed `.range()` is the sole mechanism that adds `limit`/`offset` to the outgoing request — so `select("*")` alone sends an unbounded request that PostgREST silently truncates to `max_rows` (1000, per supabase/config.toml:10) with a plain 200 and `error === null`, exactly as the finding describes. The codebase itself independently corroborates this failure mode: lib/server/health-daily.ts explicitly documents the identical truncation bug having hit `health_samples` before ("T11b audit finding 2") and had to build a keyset-paginated loop specifically to avoid it — the backup route never got that fix. I confirmed no test file exists for this route. I did not find a reason to doubt the claim; I could not run this against a live >1000-row table (read-only constraints, no production writes, no full suite), but the mechanism is proven at the library-source level plus a same-codebase precedent, which is about as strong as non-live evidence gets.

I do adjust severity from critical to high. The rubric's "critical" bucket is data loss / safety-rule violations / auth bypass happening now. This bug does not itself delete or corrupt Sasha's live data — it makes one of two backup paths silently incomplete. The route's own top comment (route.ts:2-8) states the *real*, acceptance-criterion-measured backup is scripts/backup.sh's `supabase db dump --db-url ...` on the Mac, which talks to Postgres directly and is NOT subject to PostgREST's max_rows at all — so a second, independent, unaffected backup already exists for the same tables. Actual data loss from this bug requires two things to both be true: (1) a table already over 1000 rows AND (2) an actual restore being needed from specifically the Vercel-cron JSON dump (e.g., because the Mac backup was also unavailable). That's a real, high-severity latent defect — a "silent failure on a [secondary] main path" that reports false success — but not the same class as an active, unconditional data-loss or auth bypass, so "high" fits better than "critical."

The technical claim (no .range()/.limit() in the TABLES loop, PostgREST max_rows=1000, and health-daily.ts's own paging precedent for the exact same truncation hazard) checks out — that part is accurate. But the impact framing collapses under the 'does it matter' lens: this route is NOT wired to any scheduler. vercel.json's crons array lists only media-sweep, oura-pull, estimate, weekly-proposal and weekly-review — /api/jobs/backup has no entry. Nothing else in the repo calls it either (no GitHub Actions cron, no pg_cron reference, no other scheduler found in .github/workflows, scripts/, or launchd/). The project's own production-readiness audit, dated 2026-09-12 (one day before HEAD), already caught and documented exactly this — "/api/jobs/backup has no cron entry in vercel.json ... so no cron ever calls it" — flagged as an open owner-decision item, explicitly noting it "may be intentional (the Mac script is the backup of record)." That matches the route's own docstring: the artifact acceptance criterion 13 actually measures is scripts/backup.sh's `supabase db dump` (a direct pg_dump against Postgres), which bypasses PostgREST entirely and is not subject to max_rows — so the backup Sasha would actually restore from is unaffected by this bug. Today there is no nightly execution to silently do anything: the route only runs on a manual POST with the correct bearer secret, there is no unattended path, and the primary/measured backup mechanism doesn't share the defect. The finding's central claims — "nightly cron", "automated, unattended... the one the acceptance criterion actually measures", "a successful nightly backup can quietly be missing... for months" — are not true of the current system. The missing pagination is a real, worth-fixing latent defect for IF this route is ever wired to a schedule and relied on for restores, but it has zero live exploitation path today and the scheduling gap it depends on is already tracked by the project's own audit trail as an open item, not a silent critical failure in production.

confirmed.title: Rotation is not actually a pure function of date — Avoid/Eats edits rewrite past days' meals
confirmed.evidence: poolFor (lib/rotation.ts:23-29) calls rotationPool(dayType, slot, target, foods) with whatever `foods` is passed in "right now"; rotationPool (lib/foods.ts:321-347) builds its option list by indexing into eatsByRole(foods) (lib/foods.ts:193-202), which sorts the CURRENT status==="eats" foods alphabetically. resolveDay (lib/resolve.ts:137) calls `mealsForDay(date, stored, undefined, store.foods)` for ANY date — past or future — using the live in-memory `store.foods`, not a snapshot from that date. I reproduced this with the actual seed data: `mealsForDay("2026-08-01", undefined, undefined, seedFoods())` gives meal-1 = "Chicken breast, Jasmine rice & Almond butter"; after flipping only `eggs` to `status:"avoid"` (eggs never appeared in that day's meals to begin with) and re-resolving the SAME date, meal-1/2/3 all changed to different foods ("Chicken breast, Butternut squash & Almond butter", "Sirloin steak, Melon...", "Canned albacore, White potato...").
confirmed.scenario: Sasha eats and checks off meal-1 on Aug 1 (chicken/jasmine rice/almond butter). Two weeks later she marks an unrelated food (e.g. eggs) Avoid after a bad reaction. The next time she — or Devin, or a symptom-correlation review — opens Aug 1 in the Week tab, resolveDay recomputes that day live and now shows a completely different meal-1/2/3 for that date, with no indication anything changed. The displayed 'history' of what she ate silently rewrites itself every time the eats/avoid list changes, for every date in the app, forward and backward.
confirmed.impact: The file header and rotation.ts's own doc comment promise "the same date always yields the same meal, on any device, forever" — that promise is false the moment she edits her food list, which is the app's core Foods-tab workflow. For a colitis patient trying to correlate symptoms to specific foods, a diet log whose past entries silently change after every Avoid/Eats edit is actively harmful to the one thing the app exists to support (accurate history), and it also means two devices that sync `foods` at different times will show DIFFERENT meals for the identical past date simultaneously.
confirmed.fix: Persist the resolved meal (or at minimum a snapshot of the foods pool used) alongside `stored.eaten`/`stored.swaps` the first time a date is rendered or a slot is checked off, and have resolveDay prefer that snapshot over a live re-derivation for any date with recorded history. At minimum, freeze the rotation once a slot is marked eaten for that date.
confirmed.testGap: lib/rotation.test.ts has no test that changes `foods` between two calls to mealsForDay/resolveDay for the same date and asserts the result is unchanged — the exact scenario the task description calls out ("rotation determinism after a food is set to Avoid mid-week").

- lib/rotation.ts:124-171 (`mealsForDay`) → line ~150 calls `poolFor(dayType, slot, foods)` per slot.

Critically, the SAME index `i` is used to pick `by.protein[i%P]`, `by.carb[i%C]`, `by.fat[i%F]` — so changing `P` (e.g. one protein flipped to avoid) changes `n` (the lcm), which changes `rotationIndex(date, n, slot)` (rotation.ts:73-77, `n % poolSize`), which reselects a different combination across ALL THREE roles, not just the one whose status changed.
- StoredDay (lib/types.ts:133-147) has no field that snapshots a resolved meal — only `swaps` (an explicit override id), `eaten` (a timestamp), `notes`. Nothing freezes what was actually shown/eaten.

- Reproduced live with tsx against `seedFoods()`: for date 2026-08-01, meal-1/2/3 = "Chicken breast, Jasmine rice & Almond butter" / "Prosciutto, Sweet potato & Avocado mayo" / "Ahi tuna, White rice & Almond butter", eggs not present in any of them. After flipping only `eggs.status` to `"avoid"` and re-resolving the SAME date with the SAME stored data, all three meals changed: "Chicken breast, Butternut squash & Almond butter" / "Sirloin steak, Melon (cantaloupe) & Avocado mayo" / "Canned albacore, White potato & Almond butter" — exactly matching the finding's reported repro output.
- Checked the guard: lib/rotation.test.ts's "is stable — same date always gives the same index" test (line 58) and rotation-variety.test.ts's determinism test only exercise `rotationIndex`/`mealFor` with `foods` omitted (falls back to the fixed authored library via `getMealOptions`, rotation.ts:28). No existing test passes a `foods` map and varies its eats/avoid status across two resolutions of the same date — the "pure function of date" doc comment (rotation.ts:8-10, 121-122) is untested for the actual `foods`-driven path and is false for it.

The claimed mechanism, reproduction, and "no guarding test" assertion all check out exactly as stated. confirmed.title: Local food-db.json ships wrong/missing off-plan flags for well-known gluten and dairy foods
confirmed.evidence: lib/food-db.ts:26 documents flags as "Off-plan for her colitis plan: 'gluten' | 'dairy' | 'apple'. Logging is still allowed," and components/LogFoodSheet.tsx:747 renders `h.flags` directly as the search result's off-plan warning (` · off-plan: {h.flags.join(", ")}`). I checked every food-db.json entry's own USDA `sr` description against its `flags` array and found `flags: []` (no warning at all) on entries that are unambiguously gluten and/or dairy by their own description: `egg-noodles-cooked` ("Noodles, egg, enriched, cooked"), `saltine-crackers` ("Crackers, saltines"), `wheat-crackers` ("Crackers, wheat, regular"), `half-and-half` ("Cream, fluid, half and half"), `m-m-s` ("Candies, ... M&M's Milk Chocolate Candies"), `cheeseburger-fast-food` ("Fast foods, cheeseburger" — bun + cheese, zero flags), `egg-mcmuffin` ("Fast foods, english muffin, with egg, cheese" — muffin + cheese, zero flags), and `clam-chowder` ("prepared with ... 2% milk").
confirmed.scenario: She uses "Log a food" (components/LogFoodSheet.tsx) and searches "cheeseburger", "egg mcmuffin", "saltine crackers", or "egg noodles" to log something she ate off-plan or is considering. Because these entries carry `flags: []`, the search result and detail view render with no off-plan badge — the same UI that, per components/LogFoodSheet.tsx:130 ("Off-plan foods (gluten, dairy, apple) are marked"), is supposed to warn her every time.
confirmed.impact: The app's whole design stance for the general food log (as opposed to her curated Eats list) is warn-don't-block — she's allowed to log anything, but is supposed to be told when it's off-plan so she can connect it to a later flare. For exactly the class of foods most likely to actually contain gluten or dairy under a name that doesn't scream it (a fast-food burger, egg noodles, saltines, half-and-half), that warning silently doesn't fire, defeating the purpose of the flag system for a real subset of the ~470-item catalog (spot check found 8 confirmed misses, likely more).
confirmed.fix: Add a build-time assertion in scripts/build-food-db.py (or a vitest check over the whole FOOD_DB array, not just five hand-picked ids) that flags every entry whose `sr`/`name` matches the known gluten/dairy/apple keyword list and fails the build if `flags` doesn't include the expected tag — the same keyword set used in lib/catalog/off-map.ts's scanAllergens, so there is one source of truth instead of three independently-maintained keyword lists (bannedReason, food-db.json's authored flags, and off-map.ts).
confirmed.testGap: lib/food-db.test.ts's "flags gluten, dairy and apple foods but still lists them" test only checks 5 hand-picked ids (white-bread, cheddar-cheese, apple-with-skin, almond-butter, oat-milk) — all of which happen to be correct — and never iterates the full 460-item dataset to catch entries like the 8 above where the flag is simply missing.

votes.reason:
Confirmed, with the root cause corrected. I verified all 8 cited food-db.json entries directly: egg-noodles-cooked, saltine-crackers, wheat-crackers, half-and-half, m-m-s, cheeseburger-fast-food, egg-mcmuffin and clam-chowder all carry flags:[] despite being gluten and/or dairy foods (lib/food-db.json). LogFoodSheet.tsx:747 does render `h.flags` verbatim as the off-plan warning, and `hits` at LogFoodSheet.tsx:183/137 passes the DB entry's `flags` straight through with no re-derivation — so the finding's rendering claim is accurate.

I traced the actual bug past what the finding guessed: scripts/build-food-db.py:605 calls `flags(name)` using the short CURATED display name (e.g. "Half and half", "M&M's", "Egg McMuffin", "Clam chowder") — NOT the full USDA `desc` string that gets stored as the `sr` field. I confirmed with the live regex (identical between build-food-db.py:515-519 and lib/catalog-client.ts:66-70, so the finding's 'three independently-maintained keyword lists' framing is not quite right — the regex is already a single shared source, faithfully ported) that running it against `desc` instead of `name` would correctly catch half-and-half ("Cream" matches dairy), M&M's ("Milk" matches dairy), egg-mcmuffin ("muffin"+"cheese" match both), and clam-chowder ("milk" matches dairy) — 4 of the 8. The remaining 4 (egg-noodles, saltine/wheat-crackers, cheeseburger) stay broken even against the full `desc` because the keyword list uses singular "noodle"/"cracker" (regex \b boundaries don't match the plural "noodles"/"crackers") and "cheese"/"burger" as standalone words (no \b match inside the single compound token "cheeseburger"). So the real fix is `flags(desc)` at build-food-db.py:605 plus adding plural variants and compound-word cases to the keyword lists — not a three-way keyword-source unification.

I also checked whether a guard elsewhere prevents the scenario: when NEXT_PUBLIC_CATALOG_SEARCH=1 (AGENTS.md says catalog search has been ON in production since 2026-09-12), LogFoodSheet renders CatalogSearch.tsx instead of the raw `hits` list, and its online path (catalog-client.ts:140) re-derives `offPlan` via `offPlanFlags(desc+brand)` over the full USDA description from the 13,694-item Supabase catalog — this does correctly flag half-and-half/M&M's/mcmuffin/clam-chowder-type cases online. But that guard is incomplete: (a) cheeseburger, egg noodles and crackers stay silently unflagged even on the online path, since it's the same regex bug; and (b) CatalogSearch's own offline fallback (catalog-client.ts:125-133, triggered by any failed fetch or an inactive catalog version — plausible on a phone-first PWA with a bad signal) uses `offPlan: h.flags`, the exact same unfixed bundled data, with no re-scan. So the scenario is real and reachable via more than one path; it is not a hypothetical.

Confirmed, not refuted. Direct inspection of lib/food-db.json shows all 8 cited ids (egg-noodles-cooked, saltine-crackers, wheat-crackers, half-and-half, m-m-s, cheeseburger-fast-food, egg-mcmuffin, clam-chowder) carry flags: [] despite unambiguous gluten/dairy content in their own sr/name fields — matches the finding exactly.

I went further to test whether this actually reproduces for Sasha given the app's current architecture, and it does, through two paths:

(1) Offline fallback (the path the finding cites via LogFoodSheet.tsx). In production `NEXT_PUBLIC_CATALOG_SEARCH=1` is on (confirmed in docs/catalog/relevance.md:283, AGENTS.md phase table, .env.local:17), so the primary UI is components/CatalogSearch.tsx, not the legacy `hits.map`/`h.flags` block the finding cites at LogFoodSheet.tsx:747 (that block only renders when `useCatalog` is false, LogFoodSheet.tsx:166,703). But CatalogSearch.tsx explicitly falls back to the same bundled food-db.json data — with the identical missing flags — whenever `/api/foods/search` throws (network drop) or returns 503 "no active catalog version" (catalog-client.ts:88-95, CatalogSearch.tsx: "Offline results — from the foods built into the app."). This is a first-class, designed-for state, not a hypothetical, and exactly the kind of connectivity gap a phone-first PWA hits routinely.

confirmed.title: Client off-plan regex misses whole gluten words (wheat, rye, semolina, malt)
confirmed.evidence: const GLUTEN = /\b(bread|bagel|muffin|...|falafel|shepherd)\b/i; — the list has no `wheat`, `rye`, `semolina`, or `malt` token at all (off-map.ts's server-side GLUTEN regex at lib/catalog/off-map.ts:141 does include them). Verified: GLUTEN.test("Wheat Thins Original") === false, GLUTEN.test("Wheat germ") === false, GLUTEN.test("Malt-O-Meal") === false, GLUTEN.test("Rye crisp crackers") === false, GLUTEN.test("Semolina flour") === false (confirmed by running the exact regex in node). This `offPlanFlags()` is the ONLY off-plan computation for online catalog search rows (lib/catalog-client.ts:140, `toRows`) and — critically — is what LogFoodSheet.tsx uses to compute the `flags` array that gets baked into the permanently stored `LoggedFood` entry for every catalog pick (components/LogFoodSheet.tsx:286 `catalogEntry()`: `const flags = offPlanFlags(...)`) and the portion-sheet warning subtitle (components/LogFoodSheet.tsx:528, 535). confirmed.scenario: She searches the online catalog for "Wheat Thins" or a product literally named "Wheat germ" / "Rye crisps" / "Malt-O-Meal". CatalogSearch.tsx shows no "· off-plan" warning (row.offPlan is empty). confirmed.impact: For a UC patient whose diet-safety promise is 'marking, never hiding' (the file's own comment at line 64), a whole class of gluten-bearing catalog items (anything named for wheat/rye/semolina/malt without also containing a word like bread/pasta/cracker) logs completely silently as safe, both in the UI and in the permanent log record.
confirmed.fix: Reuse lib/catalog/off-map.ts's GLUTEN/DAIRY/APPLE regexes (or a single shared constant) instead of maintaining a second, narrower copy in lib/catalog-client.ts; at minimum add wheat, rye, semolina and malt to catalog-client.ts's GLUTEN regex.

confirmed.title: mineAsDb never computes off-plan flags for her own foods
confirmed.evidence: mineAsDb(f: Food) returns `{ ..., flags: [] }` unconditionally — it never runs any gluten/dairy/apple text check against `f.name`, unlike FOOD_DB rows (pre-computed `flags` from scripts/build-food-db.py) and unlike the online catalog path (lib/catalog-client.ts offPlanFlags). Since `pick()` in LogFoodSheet.tsx:354 builds the logged entry's `flags` from `picked.flags` (picked = mineAsDb(mine[id]) for source "mine"), and `searchFoods` in lib/food-db.ts:133 also hard-codes `flags: []` for every 'mine' search hit, the ONLY defense against logging an off-plan 'mine' food is the one-time `bannedReason()` gate run at add-time (components/AddFoodSheet.tsx:123, or the MCP add_food tool at app/api/mcp/route.ts:92) — there is no independent runtime check anywhere downstream.
confirmed.scenario: Any food that slips past `bannedReason()` at add time — including the already-known buttermilk/malt gaps, any future gap in that regex, or a food migrated in from an old export that predates the check — is then permanently unflagged everywhere it is searched or logged: CatalogSearch's own-food rows, the portion-sheet subtitle, the stored LoggedFood.flags, and the note sheet. Unlike the bundled-USDA and online-catalog food sources (which independently re-derive flags at search/log time from the name/ingredients, so a gap in one gate can still be caught by another), her own food list has no such second layer.
confirmed.impact: For the one food source she uses most (her own curated Eats list, per AGENTS.md the primary logging path via My Foods / BuildMealSheet / LogFoodSheet's own-food picker), a single miss in the add-time text regex is invisible forever after, with nothing else in the system positioned to catch it.
confirmed.fix: Have mineAsDb() (and lib/food-db.ts's searchFoods for `mine` hits) compute flags from `f.name` using the same off-plan detector the bundled/catalog paths use, instead of hard-coding `flags: []`, so the check is redundant rather than singular.

votes.reason:
Every cited fact checks out and the scenario reproduces end-to-end.

- lib/food-db.ts:144-172 `mineAsDb()` hard-codes `flags: []` at line 162 regardless of `f.name`; line 133's `searchFoods()` does the same for every "mine" search hit. Confirmed by direct read.
- components/LogFoodSheet.tsx:354-355 `pick(id, "mine")` calls `mineAsDb(mine[id])`; `buildEntry()` (line 374) sets `flags: picked.flags.length ? picked.flags : undefined` — always `undefined` for a "mine" pick since `picked.flags` is always `[]`.
- The only gate on a "mine" food's off-plan status is `bannedReason()` (lib/foods.ts:138), called at add-time in components/AddFoodSheet.tsx:122 (`canSave = ... && !banned`) and in app/api/mcp/route.ts:92 (`add_food` tool). No other code path (MyFoods.tsx, FoodSheet.tsx, BuildMealSheet.tsx) re-derives or displays off-plan status for a "mine" food — grep found zero matches for offPlan/bannedReason/flags logic in those three files.
- By contrast, `FOOD_DB` rows get `flags` precomputed by scripts/build-food-db.py, and the online catalog path independently recomputes them via `offPlanFlags()` in lib/catalog-client.ts:75-81 — so only the "mine" source lacks this second layer, exactly as claimed.
- The claimed regex gap is real, not hypothetical: `bannedReason("Buttermilk")` returns `null` (verified via node) because `\bmilk\b` requires a word boundary that "buttermilk" doesn't have — a Buttermilk-named food (clearly dairy) passes the add-time gate untouched. "Malt extract" similarly passes (gluten regex has no "malt" term in lib/foods.ts, though a parallel implementation in lib/catalog/off-map.ts does include it — confirming the regex logic is duplicated and inconsistently maintained across the codebase, reinforcing the "gap in one gate, uncaught" framing).
- lib/food-db.test.ts:96-98 is the only test touching `mineAsDb`, and it checks only macro conversion, not flags — this is a genuine coverage hole, not something an existing test already guards.
- Ran a live vitest repro (constructed a "Buttermilk" Food, confirmed `bannedReason` passes it, then confirmed `mineAsDb` and `searchFoods` both report `flags: []`): both assertions passed, demonstrating the exact failure chain end-to-end.

Impact assessment for severity: this bug lives in a secondary/backup layer. The primary safety mechanism (composeMeal/rotation.ts drawing meals only from the `Food.status === "eats"` list, gated by `bannedReason()` at add-time, backed by lib/foods.test.ts/lib/meals.test.ts) is untouched by this finding — a "mine" food that slips through `bannedReason()` would still silently enter meal composition regardless of `mineAsDb`'s flags (that's a distinct, more severe issue in `bannedReason`'s regex coverage, not in the code this finding targets). What this specific bug breaks is the documented "Off-plan foods are flagged, not hidden" behavior (AGENTS.md) for logged "mine" foods — a missing warning badge/label on an already-mis-added food, not a plan-safety violation, wrong numbers, or data loss. That matches "medium: edge case, degraded UX, missing coverage" in the given rubric — not high or critical.

confirmed.title: Coach confirm sheet always shows draft items as "allowed", losing real verdicts
confirmed.evidence: draftToProposeResponse (lib/coach-client.ts:111-118) hardcodes `policy: { verdict: "allowed" }` for every item it maps from a CoachDraft. The CoachDraft type itself (lib/coach/types.ts:29-33) has no verdict field at all on its items. In lib/server/coach.ts:361-363, `checkDraft(draft, profile, evidence)` computes a real per-item verdict (allowed/blocked/unverified) but the result (`draftChecks`) is used ONLY to null the *entire* draft when ANY item is 'blocked'; the per-item verdicts (including 'unverified') are never attached to `CoachDraft` or returned in `CoachTurnResponse`. The existing test (tests/coach/coach-client.test.ts:56-70) only exercises the always-'allowed' mapping and asserts it as correct, so it doesn't catch the information loss. Compounding this, CoachChat.tsx:171-177 gates the 'Log this' button on the matching *suggestion's* verdict (`s.verdict === 'allowed'`) but opens `state.draft` — the WHOLE draft object — not just that item, so tapping Log on one allowed suggestion opens every item in the draft, including any that checkDraft actually marked 'unverified'.
confirmed.scenario: Sasha asks the coach for a snack. The model calls draft_log_entry directly (nothing in lib/coach/prompt.ts requires it to call search_foods first for the same food name) for a home-style dish name that isn't in catalog_ingredients or was never separately searched in this turn. draft_log_entry's own internal grounding search (lib/coach/executors.ts:61-69) finds a real foodRefId but discards the allergenTags/category/prefStatus it fetched. Back in coach.ts, `evidence[row.name]` is empty (no matching search_foods tool call populated it), so checkDraft marks that item 'unverified' rather than 'blocked' — the draft is NOT nulled. The confirm sheet (CaptureConfirm.tsx, whose Save-button and warning-dot logic depends on `item.policy.verdict`) is fed `verdict: 'allowed'` regardless, so Sasha sees a normal, fully-green pre-filled entry with no 'Unverified' pill and taps Save.
confirmed.impact: The one place designed to warn her when the system genuinely could not verify a food ('the policy runs after the model and before render... so a client that ignores verdict cannot show an allowed-looking card', per lib/server/coach.ts's own top comment) is defeated for every coach-originated draft. She loses the honest 'we don't know' signal for a person managing ulcerative colitis and three hard-avoid allergens, even though a genuinely catalog-tagged allergen would still be caught at commit (see the next finding for where that backstop itself has a gap).
confirmed.fix: Add a `verdict`/`reason` field to `CoachDraft.items` (lib/coach/types.ts), populate it from `checkDraft`'s per-item result in lib/server/coach.ts instead of discarding it, and have draftToProposeResponse map that real verdict through instead of hardcoding 'allowed'. Also thread the draft_log_entry executor's own grounding-search allergen/category evidence into the evidence map so items drafted without an explicit prior search_foods call still get a real verdict.

votes.reason: The core factual chain checks out end to end: CoachDraft.items has no verdict field (lib/coach/types.ts:29-33); draftToProposeResponse hardcodes policy:{verdict:'allowed'} for every item (lib/coach-client.ts:115); checkDraft computes real per-item verdicts (lib/coach/policy.ts:38-53) that coach.ts only uses to null the WHOLE draft when any item is 'blocked' (lib/server/coach.ts:361-363) — the per-item verdicts (including 'unverified') are attached to policy_checks for audit persistence only, never to the CoachTurnResponse.draft field that reaches the client. draft_log_entry's own grounding search does discard allergenTags/category (lib/coach/executors.ts:59-69, only foodRefId is kept), and evaluatePolicy legitimately returns 'unverified' (not 'allowed') when allergenTags is null and onEatsList is false (lib/policy/constraints.ts:50-53) — so an item can reach draftChecks as genuinely 'unverified' without the draft being nulled, and the client then mislabels it 'allowed'. The test (tests/coach/coach-client.test.ts:56-70) does assert the hardcoded 'allowed' as correct and never exercises a non-allowed verdict, confirming the hole. So the finding is correct as a description of the code. However the severity is overstated: I verified two independent facts that bound the actual harm. (1) canSave (lib/capture-client.ts:189-192) only blocks Save on verdict==='blocked' — 'unverified' already does not block Save today, with or without this bug, so the Save button's gating behavior is unchanged by fixing it; the only loss is the 'Not checked' pill (policyCopy, lib/capture-client.ts:295-297) not rendering. (2) There is a real, independent commit-time backstop: lib/server/log.ts policyIssues (lines 382-394) re-runs evaluatePolicy against real catalog evidence fetched by food_ref_id/food_revision_id (evidenceForItems, ~370-376) on every commit, and checkLabelAndPolicy (397-406) refuses the write before any row is inserted if that recomputed verdict is 'blocked' — entirely independent of whatever verdict the confirm sheet displayed. So a genuinely allergen-tagged food is still blocked at commit regardless of this client-side bug (the finding itself acknowledges this, deferring the actual bypass scenario to 'the next finding' about the evidence-threading gap). Given no safety-rule bypass, no wrong numbers, no data/sync loss, and no change to what Save actually allows, this is a real but bounded transparency/UX defect: Sasha loses an honest 'we didn't check this' pill on some coach-drafted items, not a working safety gate.

I directly reproduced this: running the repo's actual `checkDraft` and `draftToProposeResponse` (via tsx against the project's own tsconfig, in the scratchpad, no repo files touched) on a CoachDraft item with no matching evidence entry gives `checkDraft(...) -> 'unverified'` and `draftToProposeResponse(...) -> 'allowed'` for the same item, confirming the information loss end to end. The compounding CoachChat.tsx claim is also confirmed: lines 171-178 gate the Log button per-suggestion on `s.verdict === 'allowed'` but the handler opens `state.draft` (the entire CoachDraft, via `onOpenDraft={setDraft}` in app/coach/CoachScreen.tsx:18), not the tapped item alone. lib/capture-client.ts:189-193 (`canSave`) and 295-306 (`policyCopy`) confirm the concrete UX effect: a true 'unverified' verdict would render a visible 'Not checked' pill on the confirm sheet (CaptureConfirm.tsx:37-48), while 'allowed' renders no pill at all — so the hardcoding silently removes that warning. The existing test (tests/coach/coach-client.test.ts:56-70) only asserts the hardcoded 'allowed' mapping, so it cannot catch this. I also checked the claimed commit-time backstop (lib/server/log.ts policyIssues/evaluatePolicy, called from applyLogEntry before any write) and confirmed it independently re-blocks any item whose *catalog-recorded* allergen tags match her avoid list, regardless of the coach turn's evidence — so a hard-avoid allergen with existing catalog data cannot silently get logged even with this bug. That keeps this a real, silent loss of an intentionally designed safety signal on the AI coach's main drafting/logging path for a person managing ulcerative colitis and three hard-avoid allergens, which fits 'high' (silent failure on a main path) rather than 'critical' (no proven bypass of an enforceable hard-block) or a downgrade to medium.

votes.reason: The code observation is accurate: lib/coach-client.ts:115 hardcodes `policy: { verdict: "allowed" }`, CoachDraft (lib/coach/types.ts:29-33) carries no per-item verdict, and lib/server/coach.ts:361-363 computes real per-item verdicts via checkDraft but discards them except to null the *whole* draft when any item is truly 'blocked'. draft_log_entry (lib/coach/executors.ts:61-73) does discard its internal search hit's allergenTags/category, keeping only foodRefId. All true. But the claimed "high" safety impact does not hold up: two independent mechanisms already prevent an actual allergen from reaching Sasha's log regardless of what the confirm-sheet pill shows. (1) Any item with real evidence marking it 'blocked' already nulls the entire draft server-side before the client ever sees it (lib/server/coach.ts:363), so the hardcoded-'allowed' client code can never surface a genuinely-blocked coach item — it only ever sees items that are truly 'allowed' or 'unverified' (missing evidence). (2) Independently of the coach turn and of any client-displayed verdict, every commit goes through lib/server/log.ts's policyIssues → evidenceForItems → evaluatePolicy (log.ts:376-397), which re-derives allergen tags fresh from the database by food_ref_id/revision (not from turn-scoped `evidence`, not from anything the client sent) and refuses the write (`status: "invalid"`) if a real catalog allergen match is found — this runs "on every commit" per its own doc comment (log.ts:373-375) and is what canSave/commitDraft in lib/capture-client.ts:189-192,224 rely on as the actual gate, not the client's cosmetic verdict. So the realistic failure mode is narrower than claimed: Sasha loses the advisory "Not checked" pill (lib/capture-client.ts:295-297, only pill copy affected since PolicyPill in CaptureConfirm.tsx:40 only colors 'blocked' differently — 'allowed' and 'unverified' render visually near-identically anyway) for a coach-drafted item lacking prior search_foods evidence. confirmed.scenario: Sasha wears her Oura ring and falls asleep at 11:00 PM Eastern on 2026-09-12 (bedtime_start = "2026-09-12T23:00:00-04:00", an ordinary bedtime). oura/map.ts's sample() converts this to the UTC instant "2026-09-13T03:00:00.000Z" and tags it tz='UTC'. confirmed.title: A 'gone' op result is silently dropped, leaving the local mirror row untouched
confirmed.evidence: applyResult (lib/sync/outbox.ts:259-292): only "applied", "conflict", "deleted", "unsupported" and "error" get a branch; everything else — including "gone" — falls through to `return dropOp(op); // 'gone' and 'duplicate': the op has nothing left to do` (line 291). `dropOp` (lines 301-304) for a non-SETTINGS entity is just `await deleteOp(op.op_id)` — it never calls `putRow`/`deleteRow` on the entity's mirror store. Contrast with the "deleted" branch (lines 264-276), which does call `deleteRow`/`clearPulledUserSettings` to bring the local mirror back in line with server truth. `drainOutbox` (line 349) buckets a 'gone' result into `out.dropped`, never `out.errored`, so `out.failed` stays false; `syncOnce` (lib/sync/client.ts:167-172) then calls `setLastError(null)` and `setLastSyncAt(...)` — a full success signal. The outbox test at lib/sync/outbox.test.ts:146-149 only asserts `pendingCount()` reaches 0 after a 'gone' result; it never checks the mirror row or the reported error state, so this hole is untested as well as unhandled.
confirmed.scenario: Any offline-queued `update` or `delete` op for `user_foods`, `log_entries`, `gut_log`, `recipes`, `favorites_*`, `plan_days`, `water_log`, `user_food_prefs`, or `duplicate_groups` whose entity_id the server has no row for at all (not tombstoned — genuinely never created there, e.g. because an earlier 'create' op for the same entity was itself lost to this exact same code path, or the phone's IndexedDB outbox and mirror drifted apart after a crash between two separate writes) gets `{status:'gone'}` back from `apply_sync_op` (supabase/migrations/20260919090300_phase3_sync_entities.sql:457-459). The client deletes the op and does nothing else. Concretely: she edits a custom food's allergen note while offline (an `update` op queued against a food whose original `create` never actually reached the server), later reconnects — the update op comes back 'gone', is silently discarded, `lastSyncAt`/`lastError` report success, and her edited food/log entry sits in local IndexedDB forever, never reaching the server and never reaching any other device.
confirmed.impact: Silent, permanent data loss on a main sync path with a false 'everything is sent' signal (SyncStatus reads exactly this state — see components/SyncStatus.tsx:38-42, 'Everything is sent'). For a phone-first PWA that is the sole record of her food log and allergen notes across devices, a write that never left this phone and is never flagged as failed is unrecoverable — she has no reason to suspect it, and nothing in the app ever retries or surfaces it.
confirmed.fix: In applyResult, give 'gone' its own branch: for an update/create, re-derive the row from the local op's payload and re-queue it as a fresh `create` op (base_rev: null) instead of dropping it; for a delete, since the server already has nothing, just delete the local mirror row to match. Either way, increment a counter that marks the drain as failed/needs-attention so SyncStatus does not report success, and log it via setLastError so she has a chance to notice and retry.
confirmed.testGap: lib/sync/outbox.test.ts's "drops the op on 'gone' and on 'duplicate'" test (line 146) only asserts `pendingCount()` — add an assertion on the mirror row surviving/being repaired and on `DrainResult.failed`/`errored` to catch this.

confirmed.title: Constraints save has no error handling — allergen edits vanish silently
confirmed.scenario: Sasha taps a Pill to add 'dairy' to Avoided foods, or types a food she reacted to into the avoid list, while her connection drops mid-request (a very normal phone-first-PWA moment). `fetch()` itself throws (TypeError: Failed to fetch); nothing in `save()` or the `onClick` handlers catches it, so the promise rejection is unhandled. `setStatus` is never called.
confirmed.impact: The pill she just tapped looks toggled in the DOM for a moment but the change never reaches the server and no 'Could not save' message appears — unlike every other failure branch in this same file (409, 422, non-ok response), which does set a status message. For a UC patient tracking dairy/gluten/apple avoidance, a silently-dropped edit to her constraints list is a safety-relevant gap: she believes an unsafe food is now recorded as avoided when it is not.
confirmed.fix: Wrap the fetch in try/catch (or add `.catch()` on the call sites) and set `setStatus("Could not save. Try again.")` on any network-level failure, matching the handling already present for HTTP error responses.
confirmed.testGap: none — no test in the repo constructs a fetch()-level rejection (vs. a non-ok response) for ConstraintsEditor.save()

votes.reason: Confirmed as written. `save()` (ConstraintsEditor.tsx:54-77) has no try/catch around `await fetch(...)` (line 56) or `await res.json()` (line 60), and every call site (lines 101, 118, 141-144, 158-161) invokes it as `void save({...})`/`void save(...).then(...)` with no `.catch`. A network-level failure (fetch throws, e.g. connection drop mid-request) therefore produces an unhandled promise rejection: `setStatus` is never reached, so no message appears — unlike the 409/422/!res.ok branches, which do call setStatus. I checked for mitigations and found none: no `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` or React error boundary anywhere in the repo; the service worker (public/sw.js) explicitly ignores non-GET requests (`if (request.method !== "GET") return;`), so it does not intercept, retry, or queue this PUT; and there is no test file for ConstraintsEditor at all (only server-side route tests in tests/constraints/route.test.ts), so no guard covers this. I also confirmed the safety relevance: lib/policy/constraints.ts's evaluatePolicy() reads avoid_allergens/avoid_food_ref_ids/banned_categories to block catalog search results and coach suggestions server-side, so a silently-failed edit to these fields really does leave an unsafe item unfiltered downstream. One detail in the scenario is inaccurate and should be corrected: the Pill component (components/Sheet.tsx:130-156) is fully controlled by the `active` prop derived from parent `profile` state, which is only updated via `setProfile` on a successful response — so on a network failure the pill does NOT visually toggle even momentarily; it simply does nothing, which is arguably a worse UX than the finding describes (no feedback of any kind, not even a transient false-positive). This doesn't change the core validity of the finding. `navigator.onLine`-gated `online` state (used to disable the UI) does not fully prevent the scenario since `navigator.onLine` can report true during real-world flaky connectivity/mid-request drops. Severity: "high" (silent failure on a main path) is appropriate per the rubric — not "critical" because the three floor allergens (gluten/dairy/apple) are hardcoded into DEFAULT_PROFILE and are enforced server-side independent of this editor (locked pills, 422 floor_violation), so this gap affects secondary allergens/foods/categories she is trying to add, not the core UC floor guarantee.

confirmed.title: Recipe save has no error handling — button sticks on 'Saving…' forever
confirmed.scenario: `saveRecipe` (lib/recipes-client.ts:48) calls `putRow` and `enqueue`, both of which can reject (lib/sync/idb.ts:72-74 `putRow` awaits the raw IndexedDB `put`, which throws on quota exceeded, private-browsing IDB restrictions common on iOS Safari, or a blocked DB). confirmed.scenario: In one turn the coach names several foods in its reply (e.g. answering "is a rice cake OK, and what should I eat for meal-2") -- suggestions = [{name:"rice cake", verdict:"allowed"}, {name:"grilled chicken", verdict:"allowed"}] -- but only calls draft_log_entry once, for the meal-2 items (chicken + rice), not the rice cake. confirmed.impact: Sasha reasonably reads 'Log this' as attached to the food card it sits under. confirmed.title: Morning-weight Save silently no-ops on invalid input
confirmed.scenario: Sasha taps the '+' FAB → 'Morning weight' (components/QuickActions.tsx:181-188, 190-208), types nothing (empty string), types a stray character, or the numeric input parses to 0/NaN, then taps 'Save' (line 201-207). `saveWeight` computes `parseFloat(weight)`; when the guard `Number.isFinite(lb) && lb > 0` fails, the function returns with no branch taken at all — `onLogWeight` is never called and `close()` is never called. The sheet just sits there with the same value in the box; there is no error state anywhere in QuickActions/QuickActionsMenu (grep of the file shows no `error`/`invalid` field) to render a message.
confirmed.impact: This is her one-tap daily ritual for logging morning weight (AGENTS.md: 'Fasts every morning' / weight is a tracked ritual). A mistyped or empty entry fails with zero visual feedback — no red text, no shake, no disabled-button state change — so she has no way to tell whether the tap did anything. She is likely to assume it saved and move on, silently losing that day's weight entry, which then also breaks WeightTrend/TdeeLines/ramp logic that depend on a complete weight series.
confirmed.fix: Add an inline validation message state to QuickActionsMenu's weight row (e.g. render `role="alert"` text under the input when `saveWeight` is invoked with a non-finite or non-positive value) instead of silently returning, so a failed save is visibly distinguishable from a successful one.

confirmed.title: Correction upsert never fires for HAE or Oura samples
confirmed.evidence: health_ingest_apply's insert has `on conflict (user_id, source_id, dedupe_key) do update set value = excluded.value, ... where excluded.vendor_updated_at is not null and (health_samples.vendor_updated_at is null or excluded.vendor_updated_at > health_samples.vendor_updated_at)` (lines 109-116). Neither normalizer that feeds this RPC ever sets vendor_updated_at: lib/health/normalize.ts's normalizeHealthAutoExport pushes samples with no vendor_updated_at field at all (lines 70-71 for sleep, 83-84 for every other metric), and lib/oura/map.ts's `sample()` helper (lines 16-21) takes an optional 7th `updatedAt` argument that none of its three callers ever supplies (ouraSleepToSamples lines 33/35/37/39, ouraActivityToSamples lines 52/54, ouraReadinessToSamples line 65). The spec itself documents the intended behaviour and names it as a required integration test that was never written: 'A corrected sample with a newer vendor_updated_at updates; with an older one it is skipped' (docs/specs/phase-5-body-data.md:303-304), and no lib/health/*.test.ts, lib/oura/*.test.ts, lib/server/oura.test.ts or lib/server/health-ingest.test.ts exists in the repo to catch this (confirmed empty `find lib/health lib/oura -iname '*.test.ts'`).
confirmed.scenario: Health Auto Export re-posts the same rolling hour bucket as HealthKit's totals keep completing through the day: at 2pm it sends active_energy for [1pm,2pm) as a provisional 120 kcal (dedupe_key = 'active_energy|<1pm-epoch>|<2pm-epoch>'); at 3pm it re-sends the same, now-finalised bucket at 180 kcal. Because vendor_updated_at is null on both payloads, the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE's WHERE clause is false every time, so the insert is a no-op for the existing row: health_samples keeps the stale 120 kcal forever. The same mechanism blocks an Oura re-pull that legitimately revises a sleep or readiness score after Oura's own backend finishes processing (oura/map.ts's `sample()` reuses the identical `id:type` vendor_sample_id on every pull), and blocks a corrected step_count, resting_heart_rate or body_mass reading from HAE the same way.
confirmed.impact: Steps, active energy, sleep, resting heart rate, HRV and body-mass values silently freeze at whatever was first ingested for a given hour/session and never reflect Apple Health's or Oura's own corrections. Because lib/server/health-daily.ts's mergedDays/rollUpDay is the one read path for the dashboard, the MCP tool and the Phase 6 TDEE/expenditure estimator, this feeds systematically undercounted (or otherwise stale) energy and activity numbers into everything Sasha and the coach see about her body, with no error anywhere — the ingest response even reports these as 'updated' successes at the API layer conceptually, but the DB write is actually a silent skip.
confirmed.fix: Either (a) have normalizeHealthAutoExport and lib/oura/map.ts's sample() populate vendor_updated_at from the source's own freshness signal (HAE's payload `sent_at`/receipt time for HAE rows, the Oura document's `updated_at`/pull time for Oura rows) so the existing WHERE clause can actually fire, or (b) drop the vendor_updated_at gate and let a same-dedupe-key re-send unconditionally overwrite value/unit/end_time (accepting last-write-wins, which is safe here since a resend for the same source+key is always a refinement of the same observation, not a stale replay — that's already handled separately by the payload-hash/event dedup layer).

confirmed.title: Weekly review graded on next week's empty data (UTC/local mismatch)
confirmed.scenario: Every Sunday, the weekly-review cron computes a week_start exactly 7 days ahead of the week that just ended (the week that hasn't happened yet). The AI is asked to classify 'Sasha's logged week' from all-zero future-day totals instead of the real week she just logged.
confirmed.impact: The Sunday-night coach review — meant to reflect her actual week back to her — is systematically built on empty/future data every single week, silently (the job reports success), producing a hallucinated or 'not enough data' summary regardless of how well she actually logged.
confirmed.fix: Compute weekStart in weekly-review/route.ts the same way weekly-proposal does: mondayOf(localDateIn(DEFAULT_TZ)) instead of raw UTC-day arithmetic on new Date().
confirmed.testGap: tests/coach/weekly-review.test.ts always passes weekStart/deps.latestEstimate explicitly into writeWeeklyReview and never exercises POST /api/jobs/weekly-review's own weekStartOf computation under a controlled clock.

votes.reason: Verified by reading the code and reproducing the arithmetic. weekly-review's route.ts:28-31 computes weekStart from now.getUTCDay() on the raw Date at the moment the cron fires (Monday 01:30 UTC per vercel.json's `30 1 * * 1`). Because the cron already fires after UTC midnight Monday, getUTCDay() always reads 1 (Monday), so `day=(1+6)%7=0` and weekStartOf returns TODAY's UTC calendar date unchanged — it never actually walks back to a prior Monday in this code path. Meanwhile weekly-proposal (route.ts:67-68, using estimate/route.ts's localDateIn/mondayOf) fires 30 minutes earlier at the same UTC-Monday moment, but converts to America/New_York first, which is still Sunday night (UTC-4/-5), and mondayOf() of that Sunday walks back 6 days to the Monday that started the week now ending. I reproduced both computations in Node across both DST regimes (2026-09-14T01:00/01:30Z and 2026-01-05T01:00/01:30Z): weekly-proposal's weekStart came out exactly 7 days before weekly-review's weekStart in every case (e.g. proposal=2026-09-07 vs review=2026-09-14). This is a structural, always-on offset, not an occasional edge case. I then confirmed reviewParts (lib/coach/weekly-review.ts:59-66) queries dayTotalsPrivileged for weekStart+[0..6], and dayTotalsPrivileged (lib/server/log.ts:132-139) calls the get_daily_totals SQL RPC (supabase/migrations/20260918090200_phase2_daily_totals.sql:22-28), which is a plain WHERE-filtered SELECT against the daily_totals view — a future date with no log_entries returns zero rows, not an error, so totalsFromRows produces an empty/zeroed DayTotals silently. I also checked tests/coach/weekly-review.test.ts: every test calls writeWeeklyReview directly with a hardcoded weekStart string ("2026-09-07"), never exercising the route's weekStartOf(new Date()) computation, so this defect has no test guard. The finding's mechanism, evidence, and 'every Sunday, silently' framing all hold up.

confirmed.title: "Download meals CSV" silently truncates at 5000 rows with no signal
confirmed.evidence: csvResponse(kind, opts, header, rows, notices) (app/api/export/route.ts:101-115) builds the CSV body from `header`, `rows` and `notices` only — it never writes `page.next_cursor` anywhere (not a trailing comment, not a response header). `streamed()` (line 117-161) calls this for every CSV request, and `limitParam()` (line 91-99) defaults to `MAX_LIMIT = 5000` whenever no `limit` query param is given. `components/ExportCard.tsx:5-9,59-64` builds `exportHref("meals", from, to)` with no `limit` param at all and renders it as a bare `Download meals CSV` — there is no fetch loop, no cursor follow-up, nothing that ever requests a second page. The card's own caption (line 50) promises "Everything you have logged, as a spreadsheet."
confirmed.scenario: Sasha taps "Download meals CSV" with no date range (the documented way to get "everything"). `streamMeals` returns at most 5000 `log_items` rows (one row per logged food item, not per meal — she logs several items per meal, several meals a day) and sets `next_cursor` when more exist, but `csvResponse` drops that cursor entirely and the link never asks for a second page. Once her item history passes 5000 rows — a realistic threshold within roughly a year of normal logging — the downloaded file silently stops mid-history: no trailing comment, no truncation marker, no error, and the byte count looks like a normal, complete CSV.
confirmed.impact: The one button in Settings that is supposed to hand her "everything you have logged" quietly hands her a partial file once her log is large enough, with no way for her (or anyone she shares the CSV with, e.g. a GI doctor correlating flares with food) to know data is missing. For a UC patient using this export to spot trigger foods, a silently incomplete history is actively misleading, not just an inconvenience.
confirmed.fix: Have `csvResponse` surface truncation — at minimum append a trailing `# truncated, more rows available` comment line (the same mechanism already used for the ODbL notice) when `next_cursor` is non-null, and ideally have `ExportCard` loop CSV requests via `cursor` until `next_cursor` is null before offering the download.

confirmed.title: Server-side "today" is computed in UTC, not Sasha's local day, on both AI surfaces
confirmed.scenario: Sasha is in a US timezone (any zone behind UTC). Any evening after roughly 4-8pm her local time (depending on her zone/DST), the UTC calendar date has already rolled over to tomorrow. She opens the MCP-connected coach (or chats with the AI coach) and asks 'what's on my plan today' or has it log a food/gut symptom with no explicit date. `get_day` calls `resolveDay(store, todayIso())`, which resolves TOMORROW's date: wrong day type (e.g. it answers with Wednesday's 7am-fasted-training plan while it is still Tuesday evening for her), wrong slot list, wrong targets, and the coach's own system prompt is told the same wrong 'today'. `log_gut`/`add_food` with no explicit date silently write her gut-symptom note or logged food against tomorrow's StoredDay instead of tonight's, so it never shows up on the day she actually logged it and instead pollutes a day she hasn't lived yet.
confirmed.impact: Rule (d) requires every date to render a complete, CORRECT day for that date. This silently serves and logs against the wrong calendar date for several hours every single evening, on the two surfaces (MCP tools and coach chat) that have no independent way to learn her true local date. A logged gut flare or food attributed to the wrong day corrupts exactly the trigger-tracking history the whole app exists to preserve, and the coach can confidently describe a training day/fast schedule that isn't actually today's.
confirmed.fix: Have the MCP client (and the coach request) pass Sasha's actual local calendar date (already computed correctly on the phone, e.g. via the same logic as lib/plan.ts's `localDateOnly`) as a required parameter instead of letting the server default via `new Date()`; if a per-user timezone is stored in settings, derive the server-side 'today' from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with that stored IANA timezone rather than the process's own local time.
